result.title: Trust Before Autonomy: Rethinking Agentic Remote Sensing for Crisis Response
result.summary: Agentic remote sensing is evaluated on how many questions it can answer, whereas crisis response depends on whether its answers can be relied on and how much of the decision can safely be handed to the agent. This paper argues that \emph{autonomy should be earned, not assumed}: An Earth-Observation (EO) agent should be granted autonomy in proportion to demonstrated reliability, epistemic honesty and verifiability. The position is supported by an evidential meta-analysis of twelve agentic RS/EO/GIS benchmark studies from peer-reviewed venues. Only one repeats runs, three contain unanswerable tasks and none measures calibration. Their own tables show that completed workflows are often not correct (task success exceeds tool-call correctness by up to 54pp on identical queries), that the gap to an expert trajectory widens overall with trajectory length (from 7 to 56pp), and that capability does not predict abstention (Spearman r from -0.25 to 0.50, all n.s.). The paper then contributes three EO-specific trust properties, an autonomy ladder for crisis EO tasks, and a readiness protocol that replays archived emergency activations before any live use. In this context, current evidence justifies assistive roles only.

AI.brief_summary: 这是一篇立场加元分析文章：主张遥感危机响应智能体的自主权应按可靠性、认知诚实与可验证性分级授予，元分析十二项 agentic RS/EO/GIS 基准研究，指出其普遍未测校准、任务成功与工具调用正确性最大相差 54pp、与专家轨迹的差距随轨迹变长由 7 增至 56pp、能力无法预测弃答，并提出信任属性、自主阶梯与就绪协议。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文对校准、弃答、轨迹长度下性能衰减与可验证性的评测视角，可能为 LVR/VLM 推理的停止决策、长度泛化与可信度评价提供问题表述线索，但领域为遥感危机响应、无 latent 推理机制，需较多核查。
